ky_indy_wall.blurb: A compact wall within Muir Valley, in the Red River Gorge near Rogers. Sixteen routes, almost all bolted sport with a single trad line, run from the upper 5.8s through the 5.10s and mostly into 5.11 and 5.12 territory. The faces are short and slightly overhanging, so the climbing leans technical and crimpy rather than long and pumpy, which makes it a good place to regain confidence after a day on the taller walls nearby. Rock is sandstone. Some sections left of the main face hold longer lines with a different feel. Spring days here are sunny.

ky_solarium_the.blurb: A steep sport wall in Muir Valley, seen from across the drainage opposite the Great Wall, in the Red River Gorge near Rogers. All fifteen routes are bolted, and the grades start at 5.11 and cluster in the 5.12s, with a few reaching 5.13, so it suits strong climbers who are projecting. It is one of the valley's harder venues, and more lines were still being developed. Rock is sandstone. Expect a short uphill walk on stairs and trail from the valley road, and far fewer easy options than elsewhere in the valley.

ky_pumpkin_patch.blurb: A south-facing sport crag on the Cathedral Domain property in the Red River Gorge, in Lee County. All fifteen routes are bolted, spanning roughly 5.8 to 5.12, with most of them in the 5.11 and 5.12 range. The climbing is steep and built on pockets and rails. The wall is said to stay cool for much of the day and to remain dry in rain, which helps on marginal weather days. The wider Cathedral Domain area is quieter than the busier parts of the gorge. The walk in is about ten minutes on a marked loop trail.

ky_eagle_point_buttress.blurb: A big south-facing cliff in the Northern Gorge of the Red River Gorge, possibly the tallest in the area. Fourteen trad routes run from 5.7 to 5.10, with a mix of single-pitch and multipitch lines, including a long five-pitch classic at the easier end. The orange sandstone is mostly good quality. Because it is a tall cliff with a long, unmarked, unmaintained approach along the river and then uphill, plan for route-finding, bring a full trad rack, and take care near the rim, where falls have caused serious injuries.

ky_main_wall.blurb: The principal cliff at Muscle Beach in the Northern Gorge of the Red River Gorge. Sixteen trad routes run mostly from 5.6 to 5.9, with a single 5.11 at the top end, making it a reasonable pick for moderate leaders. The wall faces mostly south with some west-facing rock, and the abrasive colourful sandstone is known for a strong run of offwidths. Crowds tend to stay away, so a partner may not appear on the trail. The approach crosses the creek and climbs through low boulders to an old logging road.

ky_three_stooges.blurb: A bouldering area in the Foxtown zone of Daniel Boone National Forest, near McKee, Kentucky. It holds fifteen problems centred on three main boulders, and most fall between V0 and V3, which makes it friendly to newer boulderers, though a handful of harder lines reach V7 and V8. It is a collection of easy-to-moderate problems and is the first group reached on the trail toward a neighbouring cluster. Bring a good brush to clean the tops of the boulders before topping out.
